title: PSYCHOLOGICAL RESPONSES TO NATURAL PATTERNS IN ARCHITECTURE
research_question: 1. Are subjective perceptions of naturalness in architectural scenes driven by objective visual patterns? 2. Do natural patterns influence similarity evaluations of architectural scenes? 3. Do natural patterns influence preference ratings of architectural scenes?

participants.description: Experiment 1: 100 American adults (55 Women, 45 men), ages 21-65 (M=34.6, SD=9.6). Half rated interiors (n=50), half exteriors (n=50). Experiment 2: 167 participants (81 from University of Chicago, 86 from New Mexico State University). Divided into 4 groups for image sets (Exteriors A n=43, Exteriors B n=41, Interiors A n=41, Interiors B n=42). Experiment 3: 100 American adults (63 Women, 37 men), ages 20-60 (M=33.3, SD=9.5). Half rated interiors (n=50), half exteriors (n=50). All participants were from the US.
participants.recruitment: Amazon's Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for Experiments 1 & 3. University of Chicago and New Mexico State University for Experiment 2.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 240 images of architectural scenes (120 interiors, 120 exteriors). Interiors from online public domain, 1000x750 pixels. Exteriors from Google Earth Street View, head-on shots 20-30 feet from façade, 1175x881 pixels. Images normalized to 4:3 aspect ratio. Minimized vegetation. 20 diverse examples for each of 6 building types (commercial, educational, government, residential, medical, religious). For Experiment 2, images resized to 360x270 pixels.

measures.instrument: Spatial Arrangement Method (SpAM), Euclidean distance between arranged images, Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) Dimension 1 weights
Combined measure of Edge Density and Fractal Dimension (calculated from Canny edge maps)
Standard deviation of Hue (sdHue), Saturation (sdSat), and Brightness (sdBright) (HSV model); Principal Component 1 (PC1) of these three for mediation analysis
Statistical measure of randomness from intensity histogram
Proportion of image area occupied by vegetation (pixel count)
Variance in MDS Dimension 1 weights predicted by naturalness ratings

mechanisms: Low-level visual patterns (Scaling, Contrast) in architectural scenes evoke intuitive associations with sensory features of nature.
Humans are innately attuned to naturalistic features of the built environment (Biophilia Hypothesis).
Nature-like patterns in architecture, resembling biological growth processes, generate aesthetic pleasure.
Softly fascinating sensory stimuli in nature (and nature-like architecture) engage attention bottom-up, replenishing cognitive resources (Attention Restoration Theory).
implementation_implications: Architects can integrate measurable nature-like patterns (Levels of Scale, Contrast) into design schemes to enhance mental health and wellbeing.
Designing with naturalistic visual patterns can create more pleasurable and restorative spaces.
Computational methods of image analysis can be used to measure and implement biophilic design features.

limitations: Reliance on 2D images as stimuli may limit generalizability to 3D built spaces.
Focus on visual perception; non-visual sensory features (e.g., acoustic, haptic, olfactory) were not assessed.
Dependent variables did not directly test psychological benefits (e.g., cognitive function, working memory tasks).
